Cooperation of Bangladesh in the investigation into Hyderabad twin blasts  
*81.    SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:†† 
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
(a) whether it is a fact that 2-day Home Secretary level talks between India and 
Bangladesh  
††The question was actually asked on the floor of the House by Shri Vijay J. Darda. 

2    Oral Answers [RAJYA SABHA]                    to Questions  
held in the month of August, 2007 agreed to take sw ift action on actionable 
intelligence on insurgents and fugitives to be shar ed between law enforcement 
agencies of the two countries; 
(b) if so, whether Government has sought the cooperatio n of Bangladesh in the 
investigation on the 25th August Hyderabad twin blasts wherein Bangladeshis have 
been held responsible; 
(c) whether those held responsible have been handed over to India; and 
(d) the steps, Bangladesh has taken to check the infiltration of Bangladeshis into this 
country? 
THE MINISTER OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRI SHIVRAJ V. PATIL): (a) to (d) A 
Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement  
(a) In the Home Secretary level talks between India and Bangladesh held in New 
Delhi on 2nd-3rd August, 2007, both sides, interalia, agreed to initiate swift action 
on information received about groups and elements a nd other fugitives from the 
law of either country taking shelter in the other country. 
(b) and (c) The case of twin blast at Hyderabad on 25-0 8-2007 is still under 
investigation by the State Police. 
(d) The issue of illegal infiltration from Bangladesh into the country has been taken 
up by the Government with the Government of Banglad esh at various fora. The 
Government has no inputs about the steps taken by t he Government of Bangladesh 
to check the infiltration of Bangladeshis into the country. 
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Sir, the hon. Minister has given the reply but I am not 
satisfied with that. What action has the Government  taken during the year 2007 to 
pursue with the Government of Bangladesh of the clo sure of training camps in its 
territory which have been imparting training to ins urgents and jihadis and what has 
been the result of such an interaction in the reduc tion of the number of militants' 
camps in the last ten months? 
SHRI SHIVRAJ V. PATIL: Sir, we are dealing with a foreign country and we have a 
mechanism for discussing such issues with Bangladesh. The issues are discussed at 
three levels. One level is that of the DGs, the Director Generals of Police; the second 
level is that of the Joint Secretaries and the third level is that of the Secretary in the 
Home Department here and the Interior Ministry over  there. They have been 
discussing these issues. But the reply we get from them is that there are no insurgents 
or terrorists having their camps over there and that if those facts are brought to their 
notice, they will take action. We have been exchang ing information between the 
Governments, giving information about the camps and  yet, unfortunately, it has 
not been possible to see that some effective action  is taken. What we get is the 
denial. We are in the process of discussing these m atters at higher levels also. At 
the Home Ministers' level this matter has been disc ussed; at the External Affairs 
Ministers' level, this matter has been discussed; at the Prime Minister's level also, 
this matter has been discussed,

SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: Sir, the Home Minister s aid in his reply 
that at the Home Secretary level talks between Indi a and Bangladesh both sides 
agreed to initiate swift action on information rece ived about militant groups. So, I 
would like to ask the Minister, Sir, whether it is true that the investigators have come 
across links between the blasts in Hyderabad this y ear and the organisations in 
Bangladesh and had sought the assistance of their counterparts in tracking down the 
origin of the phone calls in the neighbouring count ry; also, whether it is true that 
the Home Ministry had received information from sec urity agencies about the 
detention of Mohammad Hamza, a key functionary of H UJI and prime suspect in

Interpol notice for Hamza. 
SHRI SHIVRAJ V. PATIL: Sir, we have been discussing  this matter with 
Bangladesh. As far as Interpol notice is concerned,  there is an international 
agreement and we follow that international agreemen t and it is expected that the 
States, the Governments of the different countries do help them. We are in the 
process of investigating into the matters relating to the incidents in Hyderabad. It 
will be premature, at this stage, to disclose the information because disclosure of the 
information, at mis stage, will affect the case. We  do have some clues and we are 
following those clues. We have given the informatio n relating to those to our 
neighbouring States and we hope that we will get the assistance and cooperation.

Joint strategy for countering threats from various militant groups 
*82 SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: Will the Minister of  HOME 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that a 3-day annual conference  of Director-Generals and 
Inspector-Generals of Police, organized by the Inte lligence Bureau was held in the 
month of October, 2007 to discuss a joint strategy with police chiefs from all States, 
para-military forces and security agencies on countering threats from various militant 
groups;  
(b) whether top officials have sought a policy for close monitoring of procedures for 
providing security to various persons; 
(c) if so, the outcome of the conference held; and 
(d) the concrete steps being taken to meet the threat of terrorists in various 
States? 
THE MINISTER OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRI SHIVRAJ V. PATIL): (a) to (d) A 
Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement  
(a) Yes, Sir. The Annual Conference of Directors Genera l of Police/Inspectors 
General of Police of States/UTs and Heads of Central Police Organizations was held 
from October 3 to 5, 2007 in New Delhi. 
(b) The issue of VVIP Security was also discussed in the Conference. 
(c) This Conference is held every year to deliberate on  new challenge, exchange 
ideas on best practices and formulate strategies an d measures to strengthen various 
aspects of management of internal security. 
(d) The Government reamins fully committed to combating  the menace of 
terrorism. The policy of the Government is to count er the challenge posed by 
terrorism by way of a multi-pronged strategy. In pu rsuance of this strategy, the 
Government has taken various measures on political, legal, security and development 
fronts. The Government is willing to talk to all th ose groups who agree to abjure 
violence and surrender arms within the framework of  the Indian Constitution. The 
Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 as amended in September, 2004 has the 
necessary provision to deal with various aspects of  terrorism. On the security front, 
the counter terrorism measures include effective bo rder management to check 
infiltration across the borders, deployment of Cent ral Forces to aid the State Police 
Forces in areas prone to terrorist violence, height ened vigil and security 
arrangements in vulnerable areas and around vital i nstallations, strengthening of 
intelligence gathering and sharing capabilities, particularly at the cutting edge level, 
augmentation and modernization of police forces and  raising of India Reserve 
Battalions ensuring improved technology, weaponry and equipment with the Central 
and State Police Forces and steps taken to achieve bilateral and multi-lateral 
cooperation to deal with the global imperatives of terrorism. 
SHRI SHIVRAJ V. PATIL: Sir, some of the hon. Member s had expressed some 
apprehensions about investigations and all those things. That is also being looked into. 
When it is taken up, we will discuss it. The Govern ment is willing to participate in 
the discussion at any time, in accordance with your directions.

of the House.

SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: Sir, one of the greatest  challenges facing 
the country today is the threat from Maoist violence, which has taken over 400 lives. It 
is almost three times more than those lost in Jammu and Kashmir. But, Sir, there does 
not seem to be a comprehensive strategy against thi s Left-wing extremism. Andhra 
Pradesh has its own strategy; Chhattisgarh has its own strategy, and so on and so 
forth. 
Sir, since the problem cuts across State boundaries, and the States would need to 
pursue a coordinated approach to meet this challenge, has the Government established 
a functional inter-State mechanism under the Intell igence Bureau or any other 
agency to tackle the threat of terrorism in a more concerted manner? 
SHRI SHIVRAJ V. PATIL: Sir, this is a very good question. Sir, we have the central 
agencies collecting the information. And the information collected by the agencies is 
shared with the State Governments. This is one steps we are taking. 
The second step which we have taken is this. For th e information of this august 
House, I would like to say that 33 battalions of pa ramilitary forces are given to the 
States which are affected by the naxalite movement.  There are 33 battalions. It is 
nearly equal to 30.000 men and officers. 
Then, we have asked the State Governments to have a  unified command. That is, 
we are not in a position to deploy the forces which are given to the State Governments. 
So, when the forces are given to the State Governme nts, they shall have to deploy 
the State Police as well as the union police in a manner they like. The liberty is given 
to them, and it is expected that the Chief Minister of the State would head the unified 
command and give directions to them. 
The third thing which we have done is that we have identified the districts which are 
affected by the naxalite movement. And, we are not only trying to deal with the police 
forces, or with the gun and the bullet, but are giv ing extra funds to the State 
Governments to develop those districts. Funds are g iven over and above what is 
already given to them. Not only that, we have given  them the UAV in Chhattisgarh 
which is the worst affected State. And allow me to say this that I do not want to take 
any political stand as such. Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand are the two States because of 
which more than 50 per cent of incidents and deaths are taking place. It is only because 
of these two States. And, these two States are the States which are contributing to the 
naxalite activities. When the naxalite activity in Andhra Pradesh has come down by 60 
per cent, the naxalite activity in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand has gone up by more 40 
per cent and 50 per cent. Incidents and deaths are taking place. We are helping them 
also. ...(Interruptions)...  
DR. MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI: Does it mean that the naxa lites have been 
exported to Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand? ...(Interruptions)...  
SHRI SHIVRAJ V. PATIL: Let me complete ...(Interruptions)... I will reply to your 
question. ...(Interruptions)... I will reply to our question. ..(Interruptions).. I am 
giving the facts. ..(Interruptions)... I am giving the facts. ...(Interruptions)... I am not 
blaming any Government. ..(Interruptions).. I am giving the facts. ..(Interruptions).. 
The fact is this. Now, this has to be understood. M oreover, we have asked the State 
Governments to recruit more persons in their police. Some of the State Governments 
are having 10,000 vacancies in the police. If you h ave 10,000 vacancies in police 
force, which has 50,000 men, how can you manage these thing? And, we are expected 
to manage from here. Suppose, we try to manage from  here, naturally, the objection 
will be raised by you only saying that constitutionally we cannot do anything. We are 
living in a federal system. The Constitutional arra ngement does not allow it. But, 
whenever we come to this House, everything which ha s to be done by the State is 
expected to be done by the Union Government. When the Union Government is try to 
act in a correct manner by helping them, you say that we have not done this thing and 
that thing. If the other stand is taken when you as k the Union Government to 
interfere in one State, naturally, you would expect us to

interfere in some other State also. And if this con tinues then the Constitutional 
arrangement has to be changed; that is why, this is  the position. Let me tell you, 1 
have given the information not in writing but in book form, graphs are given which go 
to show in which State Naxalite activities have gone up and in which State Naxalite 
activities have come down. My humble request to the hon. Members is to just look at 
these four, five charts only, which will not take e ven two minutes. It will give you 
the information relating to what is actually happen ing, where it is happening and 
what has to be done by the State. 
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: Sir, actionable intellig ence is the only 
way to foil any threats from the terrorist groups w ho are using modern technology 
and very sophisticated weapons. My question is: Whe ther the Ministry of Home 
Affairs has drawn up a plan for modernisation of ga dgets and technologies that are 
used for intelligence gathering. Though I know you have Constitutional handicaps 
and restrictions, I would like to know whether the States have been asked to draw up 
similar plans. Though the Central has allocated a l ot of funds for the States, in the 
past, the Home Minister had said that the States ha ve not fully utilised those funds. 
So, what plans do you have and how do you propose t o ensure that the States 
upgrade their gadgets and technologies, because, ot herwise, the war on terrorism 
cannot be fought effectively? 
SHRI SHIVRAJ V. PATIL: This is exactly what we have done, Sir. Now, we are 
strengthening the intelligence agencies at the national level — the defence intelligence — 
RAW, IB and all those things. That information is collected. Then, collectively, that 
information is scanned. Thereafter, the relevant in formation is passed on. For this 
purpose, modernisation scheme is drawn up, and that  scheme is being implemented. 
But, this is not enough. It is necessary for the St ate Intelligence Departments to 
strengthen themselves. That is why, we have prepared, some suggestions and given 
to them, as to what kind of equipment they should p rocure, what kind of training 
they should give, how many people they should have in the special branches, and if 
the officers are not ready to work in the special branches, what special facilities should 
be given to them and all those things. So, information has been given to them. I .am 
happy to inform the House that some States have realised that if Naxalite activity or 
terrorist activity, or any violent activity is to be controlled, then, more than the gun, 
the intelligence is important. They should rely upo n intelligence. They are 
strengthening their intelligence agencies. For inst ance, Andhra Pradesh is doing, 
Maharashtra is doing, Karnataka is doing, Tamil Nadu is also doing something and 
some other States are also doing it. But the movement in this direction, started by the 
State Government, is a little slower. We are giving a lot of funds to them. We are asking 
them to have a holistic plan, so that, not only the intelligence and training but also the 
back up of the action, which has to be taken, shoul d be considered. We have asked 
them to prepare the plans themselves in consultation with the Union Government as to 
how the plan should be refined, also in consultatio n with the adjoining State 
Government and do it. So, we are also helping them in every respect, but direct action 
is not permitted by the constitution. Excepting direct action, any other help which is 
required by the State Government is being given.

Eradication of child labour  
*91. SHRI O.T. LEPCHA: Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of policy initiative measures that have been taken or proposed to be taken 
by Government to eradicate child labour in the country; 
(b) the details of efforts made so far by Government in this respect; and 
(c) the details of schemes formulated and being impleme nted by Government 
alongwith the funds allocated for the purpose in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND  
EMPLOYMENT (SHRI OSCAR FERNANDES): (a) to (c) The National Policy-on Child 
labour envisages strict enforcement of the Child Labour (Prohibition & Regulation) Act, 
1986 with simultaneous efforts towards rehabilitation of both parents and children through 
a project based action plan linkages with the poverty eradication and income generation 
programmes of the Government. Considering the magnitude and nature of the problem, 
Government is following a gradual and sequential approach of initially covering children 
working in hazardous occupations and process. Under the Child Labour (Prohibition & 
Regulation) Act, 1986 there are 15 occupations and 57th process banned for the 
employment of children below the age of 14 years. State Governments are the appropriate 
authority for the enforcement of the Act for the arexs under their jurisdiction. 
For the rehabilitation of child labour Government is implementing the National Child 
Labour Project (NCLP) Scheme in 250 districts of the country. Under the Scheme, children 
withdrawn from work are admitted into special schools, where they are provided with 
education, vocational training, mid-day meal, stipend and health care facilities etc. In 
addition, INDUS Child Labour Project, a jointly funded Project of Government of India 
and US Department of Labour is also being implemented in 21 districts. Government is 
also implementing a Scheme of Grants-in-aid to Voluntary Organization in the districts, 
which are not covered under NCLP/INDUS Projects. An amount of Rs. 175 crores has been 
allocated for the purpose under these schemes during the current financial year.

The Ministry of Labour and Employment is regularly monitoring the implementation of 
these schemes through periodical reports, visits, inspections and review meetings. The Central 
Monitoring Committee on Child Labour headed by Union Labour Secretary, with Labour 
Secretaries of all States implementing the child labour schemes as members, reviews in detail 
the implementation of these schemes by the State Governments and suggests corrective action 
wherever necessary. 
For the 11th Plan, the Ministry has proposed expansion of the NCLP Scheme to 600 
districts of the country. In addition, certain other additional features in the Scheme have also 
been proposed, viz. residential schools for migrant children in big cities, vocational training for 
adolescents in the age group of 14 to 17 years, greater State level monitoring and awareness 
generation. 
Last year, Government took a major step towards the elimination of child labour by banning 
the employment of children as domestic servants and in dhabas, hotels, roadside eateries. A 
large number of children all over the country are working in these two occupations. 
The Ministry is taking various measures to cover the families of child labour under the 
developmental schemes of other Ministries to help in their economic upliftment so that 
they are not compelled to send their children to work. A Core Group on Convergence has 
also been formed under the Chairpersonship of Union Labour Secretary involving other 
Ministries concerned viz. Human Resource Development, Women & Child Development, 
Rural Development, Urban Housing and Poverty Alleviation, Social Justice & Empowerment, 
Health etc., so that these families can get the benefit of the Schemes of these ministries also. 
The ministry is also regulairly conducting awareness generation campaigns on the issue. 
Recently, beginning from 14th  November, 2007, the Ministry has launched a fortnight long 
drive to step up enforcement of the Child Labour (Prohibition & Regulation) Act. The 
State Governments have been requested at the level of Chief Ministers to bake all necessary 
measures for ensuring legal compliance and creation of mass awareness against the evil of 
child labour. Funds have also been allocated to them specially for carrying out awareness 
generation campaign during the period.

implement drinking water suply schemes in such villages. This programme continued 
till 1973-74, but with the introduction of the Mini mum Needs Programme (MNP)

Written Answers to [21 NOV. 2007]   Starred Questions     37 
THE MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (DR. RAGHUVANSH 
PRASAD SINGH): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. Review of the progress of the implementation 
of NREGA is done on regular basis NREGA has been re viewed at the highest level 
in Prime Minister's review meeting on 20.6.2007. Pe rformance Review Committee 
meetings are undertaken by the Minister of Rural Development and Secretary (Rural 
Development) from time to time. During the year 200 7-08, three Regional Review 
Committee meetings have been held to cover review o f all States. These were held 
at Orissa, Guwahati and Jaipur. A Central Employmen t Guarantee Council was 
constituted on 22.9.2006 to review and monitor the implementation of the Act. The 
Council has so far held three meetings and reviewed  the implementation of 
NREGA. Members of the Council also conduct field visits in various States to oversee 
the progress of the Act. An Executive Committee con stituted under the Central 
Council reviewed the progress of the Act in its meeting held on 16.8.2007.

Parliament held during 20th - 23rd August, 2007 and  5th -6th September, 2007. 
National Level Monitors (NLMs) and Area Officers of  the Ministry visit various 
districts to oversee the progress of the Act. the A rea Officers have been directed to 
cover 10 village during their each visit. Vigilance and Monitoring Committees have 
also been set up to review the implementation of the Act.

varies from State to State based on the scale and v olume of demand in a particular 
context. During the year 2006-2007, a total of 2.12 crore households had demanded 
employment, out of which, 2.10 crore were provided employment. During the current 
year upto September, 2007 a total of 1.98 crore hou seholds have demanded 
employment, out of which, 1.88 crore have been provided employment. However, in 
some States the implementation of the Act has been affected due to State Assembly 
elections and also due to natural calamities like r ains, floods etc. As employment is

(DRDO), had conducted two studies. One on the "Psycho-Social aspect of optimizing the 
operational efficiency of Security Forces to combat insurgency" during September 2000—
May 2005 in the North Eastern Region. The major outcomes of the study are: 
(i) Three main operational stressors, like fear of torture, uncertain environment and 
domestic stresses are responsible for most of psychological problems in various 
group of Armed Forces. 
(ii) Middle rank Officers as compared to Jawans and  Junior Commissioned 
Officers (JCO) were found to be more vulnerable and stressed out 
(iii) Mental disorders in the form of Post Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) have

symptoms.

appropriate period to change in the attitudes of youth and influence their minds 
towards national identification.

Management training Programmes. 
(vi) Need for immediate therapeutic intervention during post-traumatic stress disorders 
jointly by unit leaders and professional psychologists. 
(vii) There is a strong need to carry out an appropriate need analysis with respect to 
demographic variables of a particular region.

troops deployed in counter insurgency areas" and su ggested a number of remedial 
measures to deal with stress related issues in the Army. Some of the suggestions are: 
liberalized leave policy, deployment of psychological counsellors in counter surgency 
areas, periodical review, monitoring and analysis of stress related incidents, organizations of 
stress management training programmes and disseminations of reading materials on stress 
management in appropriate languages, etc.

†335. SHRI KESHUBHAI S. PATEL: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be 
pleased to state:

inside the country and on the borders in the country;

not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAI RS (SHRI 
SHRIPRAKASH JAISWAL): (a) to (c) The Govt. is aware of the challenge posed by 
terrorism, which has now become a global phenomenon . The Government remains 
fully committed to combating the menance of terrori sm by way of a multi-pronged 
strategy. In pursuance of this strategy, the Government has taken various measures on 
political, legal, security and development fronts. The Government is willing to talk to 
all those groups who agree to abjure violence and s urrender arms within the 
framework of the Indian Constitution. The Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 
1967 as amended in September, 2004 has the necessar y provisions to deal with 
various aspects of terrorism. On the security front , the counter terrorism measures 
include effective border management to check infilt ration across the borders, 
deployment of Central Forces to aid the State Polic e Forces in areas prone to 
terrorist violence, heightened vigil and security a rrangements in vulnerable areas and 
aound vital installations, strengthening of intelli gence gathering and sharing 
capabilities, particularly at the cutting edge leve l, augmentation and modernization 
of police forces and raising of India Reserve Batta lions, ensuring improved 
technology, weaponry and equipment with the Central  and State Police Forces, and 
steps taken to achieve bilateral and multi-lateral cooperation to deal with the global 
imperatives of terrorism. Rise in suicide cases in the country

Increase in kidnapping for ransom  
341. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT: Will the Minister of HOME  AFFAIRS be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that incidents of kidnapping f or ransom and killing have 
increased during the last two years; 
(b) if so, the details of cases during the last five years; 
(c) in how many cases the police could rescue the victim and arrest the culprits and 
cases where it failed; and 
(d) what special steps are proposed to be taken to prevent kidnapping of innocent 
people? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAI RS (SHRI 
MANIKRAO GAVIT): (a) As per information obtained from the State Governments/ 
Union Territory Administration and compiled by the National Crime Records Bureau 
(NCRB) a total of 813 and 630 cases of kidnapping and abduction for ransom was reported 
in the country during the years 2005 and 2006 respectively, thus showing a declining 
trend. NCRB does not maintain data on kidnapping for killings. 
(b) The State/UT-wise details of cases registered under kidnapping and abduction for 
ransom during 2002 to 2006 have been indicated at Statement-I (See below) 
(c) State/UT-wise details of cases registered, cases chargesheeted, cases convicted, 
persons arrested, persons chargesheeted and persons convicted under kidnapping and 
abduction during 2002 to 2006 have been indicated at Statement-II (See below) 
(d) 'Police' and 'Public Order' are State subejcts under the Seventh Schedule to the 
Constitution of India and therefore, the State Governments are primarily responsible 
for prevention, detection, registration and investi gation of crime including 
kidnapping of innocent people and for prosecuting t he criminals through the 
machinery of their law enforcement agencies. The Mi nistry of Home Affairs, 
however, supplements the efforts of the State Gover nments by providing them 
financial assistance for modemization  of their Police Forces in terms of weaponry, 
communication, equipment, mobility, training and ot her infrastructure under the 
Scheme of Modernization of State Police Forces. Fur ther, intelligence inputs are 
regularly shared by the Central Security and Intelligence Agencies with the State Law 
Enforcement Agencies to prevent crime and law and order related incidents. The State 
Governments are also advised from time to time to g ive more focused attention to 
improving the administration of criminal justice sy stem and take such measures as 
are necessary for the prevention of crimes.

Cases of people taking law into their hands  
342. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the country is drifting towards anarchy as people have 
started taking law into their hands and settling is sues in public without involving 
police or judicial process; 
(b) if so, the details thereof and the reason therefor; 
(c) the details of such incidents that have come to the notice of Government during 
last one year; and 
(d) the reaction of Government thereto? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAI RS 
(SHRI SHRIPRAKASH JAISWAL): (a) to (c) No, Sir. How ever, in the recent 
past, some incidents of mob violence have come to notice in the States of U.P. Bihar, 
Rajasthan,Haryana, W. Bengal, M.P, Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh. 
(d) As per the Constitution 'Public Order and 'Poli ce' are State subjects and it is 
primarily the responsibility of the State Govts, to maintain law and order in their States 
and ensure safety and security of their people. How ever, in the wake of incidents of 
mob violence, all States/ UTs have been advised by the Central Govt  on 19.9.2007 to 
adequately sensitize their police forces so that mo bs are not allowed to indulge in 
violence, and the action taken by the police against the persons/prepetrators of such 
violence be given wide publicity so as to deter such incidents.

and research programmes for stakeholders, including Government functionaries, and 
undertake training of faculty members of the State level training institutes. It may also 
provide any other assistance as may be required by the State Governments of the State 
training institutes for capacity building of stakeh olders, Government including its 
functionaries, civil society members, corporate sector and people's elected representatives.

or other training institutes identified by the Stat e Governments in operation of a 
faculty/centre of disaster management for training and orientation of Government functionaries

for building up of the capacity of engineers and architects in earthquake risk management 
are also under implementation in all the States. The State Governments have also been 
advised to develop Search & Rescue teams by convert ing the existing 
companies/battalions of the State Forces. They have been requested to procure necessary

Increase in Unemployment 
371. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the Minister of LABOUR AND 
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether with economy registering a regular growth o f 7 to 9 percent every 
year, unemployment has out-stripped all economic growth; 
(b) if so, the comparative figures of economic growth, growth in employment and 
unemployment over the last three years, indicating the number of the unemployment 
generated both in rural and urban sector during these years; and 
(c) the main reasons for increase in unemployment and t he concrete steps 
proposed to be taken to deal with this menace? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND  
EMPLOYMENT (SHRI OSCAR FERNANDES): (a) and (b) Reli able estimates of 
employment and unemployment are obtained through quinquennial labour force survey 
conducted by National Sampled Survey Organisation a nd estimates of Gross 
Domestic Product (GDP) are obtained through Nationa l Accounts Statistics 
compiled by Central Statistical Organisation. As pe r these reports, the Indian 
Economy registered an average annual growth rate of 6.7% during 1993-94 to 1999-
2000 and 5.98% during 1999-2000 to 2004-2005, whereas the annual rates of growth 
of employment as on usual status basis during these  periods were 0.98% and 2.95% 
as against unemployment growth rate of 3.23% and 3. 7%. Number of unemployed 
persons was estimated to have increased from 9.04 m illion in 1999-2000 to 10.84 
million in 2004-05, resulting into an increase of 1 .80 million (1.15 million in rural 
and 0.65 million in urban areas). 
(c) Increase in unemployment is mainly attributed t o higher rate of growth of 
working age population than total population, incre ase in labour force participation 
rates, particularly among women and higher unemploy ment among educated youth. 
Approach paper to 11th Five Year Plan envisages cre ation of 70 million job 
opportunities during the Plan period and in order t o achieve this target, rate of 
growth of non agricultural employment is to be accelerated to 5.8% per annum from 
4.7% in 1999-2005.

Grant of concessions to textile exporters 
403.  SHRI B. J. PANDA: 
MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR: 
Will the Minister of TEXTILES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government proposes to grant certain concessions to textile exporters to 
overcome the problems being faced by them as a resu lt of appreciation of rupee 
against Dollar; 
(b)if so, the details thereof, inter-alia indicating its status in Orissa;

US$ 25.06 billion. It is hoped that the textiles industry would be making sincere efforts

Statement-I 
Details of Technology upgradation Fund Scheme                                 
(i)    The rate of interest reimbursement on spinning machinery has been reduced to                     
4%. All the remaining sub-sectors covered under the scheme would continue to get 
assistance® 5%. 
(ii) The scheme will continue to provide cover for foreign exchange rate 
fluctuation not exceeding 5%. However, for the spin ning machinery the 
coverage will be 4%. 
(iii) The Scheme will now provide an additional opt ion to the powerlooms units 
to avail of 20% Margin Money subsidy under TUFS in lieu of 5% interest 
reimbursement on investment in TUF compatible speci fied machinery 
subject to a capital ceiling of Rs. 100 lakh and ceiling on capital subsidy Rs. 
20 lakh. A minimum of 15% equity contribution from beneficiaries will be 
ensured. 
(iv) The Scheme will not provide 15% Margin Money s ubsidy for SSI textile 
and jute sector in lieu of 5% interest reimbursemen t on investment in TUF 
compatible specified machinery subject to a capital ceiling of Rs. 100 lakh 
and ceiling on capital subsidy Rs. 15 lakh. A minum um of 15% equity 
contribution from beneficiaries will be ensured. 
(v) The Scheme will continue to provide 5% interest  reimbursement plus 10% 
capital subsidy for specified processing machinery. 
(vi) The Scheme will now provide 5% interest reimbu rsement plus 10% capital 
subsidy for specified machinery required in manufacture of technical textiles and 
garmenting machineries. 
(vii) The Scheme will now provide interest subsidy/capital subsidy/margin money 
subsidy on the basic value of the machineries and exclude the tax component 
for the purpose of valuation in view of the decisio n for non-subsidizing the 
taxes. 
(viii) The Scheme will provide 25% capital subsidy on purchase of the new 
machinery and equipments for the pre-loom & post-loom operations, 
handlooms/up-gradation of handlooms and testing & Q uality Control 
equipments, for handloom production units. 
(ix) The entire range of imported second hand machi nery will not be ineligible 
under the Scheme for any benefit except automatic shuttleless looms with the value 
cap of Rs. 8.00 lakh per machine and 10 years' vintage and with a residual life of 
minimum 10 years, (x) Other investments such as ene rgy savings devices, 
effluent treatment plant, in-house R&D, IT includin g ERP, TQM including 
adoption of ISO/BIS standards, CPP etc. will now be eligible for benefits of the 
Scheme only upto 25% of the cost of machinery. 
(xi) Invesments like land, factory building, pre-op erative expenses and margin 
money for working capital will now be ineligible fo r benefit of 
reimbursement under the scheme except meant for app arel sector and 
handloom with existing 50% cap i.e. 50% of the cost  of machinery and 
equipment.

Increase in MSP for cotton 
406. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the Minister of TEXTILES be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that higher production cost of  cotton, Minimum Support 
Price (MSP) of cotton and import of cotton has exag gerated the situation of the 
farmers in Maharashtra; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that there is a big gap b etween Minimum Support 
Price and production cost of the cotton; 
(c) if so, whether Government has any proposal to incre ase M.S.P. and also 
increase of import duty on cotton; if so, the detai ls thereof; and if not, the reasons 
therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF TEXTILES ( SHRI 
E.V.K.S. ELANGOVAN):(a)No, Sir. 
(b) No Sir. The MSP is fixed by the Government of I ndia every year on the 
recommendation of Commission on Agricultural Costs & Prices (CACP) which 
takes into account the cost of cultivation per hect are, cost of production per quintal 
in various regions of the country, changes in input  prices like seeds, pesticides, 
fertilizers etc., demand and supply situation, effect of industrial cost structure, parity 
between prices paid and prices received by the cott on farmers etc., plus a reasonable 
profit margin to the cotton farmers. This mechanism 

Written Answers to [21 NOV. 2007] Unstarred Questions    135 
of fixing MSP on year to year basis helps in guaran teeing an assured price to the 
cotton fanners and sustain their continued interest  in cotton cultivation. The import 
of cotton is under Open General Licence (OGL) since  19.4.1994 without any 
qualitative or quantitative restrictions and the said policy is still being continued. The 
existing basic custom duty on import of raw cotton is 10%. Import of cotton is the 
last year was 1.78% of the total production. 
(c) MSP is fixed every year taking into account the cos t of various inputs and a 
reasonable margin of profit. There is no proposal f or increase of import duty on 
cotton. 
(d) and (e) Question does not arise in view of above.

Demolition Of A Buddhist Statue In Arunachal Pradesh By The Chinese Army 
SHRI NABAM REBIA (Arunachal Pradesh): Mr. Deputy Ch airman, Sir, 
through you, I would would like to draw the attention of the Government to an issue, 
which is of very urgent nature and also of utmost importance. Sir, a lot of intrusions, 
incursions are taking place from Chinese side in th e Indian territory, especially, in 
the State of Arunachal Pradesh and the State of Sik kim. Now, on 30th October, the 
Chinese Army ingressed into the Indian territory and demolished a Buddhist statue at 
Bum La in Tawang District of Arunachal Pradesh. I would like to know whether the 
Government of India is aware of this happening or not. 
Sir, China still does not recognize the McMahon Lin e as the border between the 
two countries. Recently, it has come out in the print media that the Chinese Advisor, 
attached to the Chinese foreign ministry has openly claimed that Tawang belongs to 
China. The claim of China is that 96,000 sq. km. area of Arunachal Pradesh belongs 
to China whereas the total area of Arunachal Pradesh is nearly 84,000 sq. kms. 
So, Sir, from the international angle, Arunachal Pr adesh still remains a disputed 
territory. We feel a lot of insecurity there and we  are not able to know as to what 
stand the Government of India is taking. We are tol d that a lot of negotiations are 
going on, a lot of discussions are going on but we are yet to know exactly what 
negotiations are going on or what discussions are going on. Recently, when the hon. 
Home Minister, Shri Shivraj Patil visited Arunachal  Pradesh, people were asking; 
Home Minister of which country is coming to Arunach al, whether he is the Home 
Minister of China or the Home Minister of India. Why are you keeping us in the dark? 
We really want to know this. Sir, we, the people of  Arunachal feel that the State of 
Arunachal Pradesh is an integral part of India, and, therefore, please do not keep us in 
the hanging position. We really want to know what e xactly is the Government of 
India doing. 
Sir, after the Chinese Army ingressed into our terr itory and demolished the 
Buddhist statue, it is reported that the Indian Arm y has just shifted the statue and 
placed it somewhere down below Tawang. Why has this act of cowardice been done 
on the part of Indian Army? Sir, nothing has come f rom the mouth of the 
Government, no reaction etc. till now. We are in a dilemma. Therefore, I want a clear 
statement on the stand taken by the Government of India on

SHRI TARLOCHAN SINGH (Haryana): Sir, it relates to honouring India's first

Sir, India's first Defence Minister, late Sardar Baldev Singh, was in the team of Pt. 
Jawaharlal Nehru when the first interim Government was formed in 1946, and he was 
taken as a representative of the Sikhs. He went with Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru and Mohd. 
Ali Jinha to represent India at the time of declara tion of Independence of the 
country in London. He refused to accept any allurem ent and declared the decision 
of the Sikh community to remain in India. This hist oric announcement led to the 
division of Punjab, and India was able to get east Punjab. Sardar Baldev Singh was 
appointed India's first Defence Minister in 1947, a nd he was responsible for 
modernising the Indian Army and handling of the attack on Kashmir by the raiders. 
Till today, nothing has been done to honour his dee ds. I request that the 
Government should at least release a commemorative postal stamp and install a 
life-size statue in the Defence Ministry campus.

Demand for setting up a Supreme Court Bench at Nagpur  
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA (Maharashtra): Sir, I am very lucky. Whenever you are in 
the Chair, I get opportunities. So, for me you are a lucky person. 
Sir, I thank you for allowing me to make my Special  Mention for setting up a 
Supreme Court bench at Nagpur. While inaugurating the first phase of the ambitious e-
courts project, interlinking of all the courts across the country on 9th July, our former 
President envisaged change in the "face of judiciar y" within the next five years. He 
advised the Supreme Court administration for fuller  utilisation of national e-
govemance, and visualised a scenario of "a citizen filling a civil dispute case using 
National ID Card and getting justice within two wee ks". Simultaneously, the Chief 
Justice of India also assured liquidation of huge arrears within a foreseeable future. 
Establishing "evening courts" introducing "plea-bar gaining system," setting up 
"fast track courts" etc., undoubtedly, contribute t owards liquidation of arrears at 
district level. Let us-also make a beginning from t he Supreme Court of India, 
functioning at Delhi, involving litigants' woes facing harrowing time chasing the apex 
court for getting justice by their constant shuttli ng from four corners of our vast 
country of Delhi. Therefore, if a bench of Supreme Court could be established at 
Nagpur, it will go a long way towards not only liquidating the pending arrears but also 
assuring quicker delivery of justice in new cases. The UPA Government under the 
inspiring guidance of its chairperson in consultati on with the Supreme Court and 
other legal luminaries may initiate a time-bound process so that Supreme Court bench 
could be established at Nagpur. A recent U.N. Repor t and the Government of India 
have already identified this city as a future metro polis. Besides its central location, 
its growing civic communicatin, aviation and power infrastructure would admirably 
fit in for setting up a bench of the Supreme Court of India at Nagpur.

Need to eradicate economic and social inequalities in India  
SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA (Andhra Pradesh): Sir, my Speci al mention relates to 
the need to eradicate economic and social inequalities in India. 
Sir, despite a glut of food and an increase in India's capacity to grow more, hunger 
remains one of India's major problems. Extreme inequalities violate the minimal level 
of social cohesion which is necessary for decency i n civic life and for the moral, 
psychological, economic and social foundations of a ny democracy. As per the 
International Food Policy Research Institute, India  is ranked at 94 out of 118 
countries in Hunger Index. Even as per the National  Commission for Enterprises in 
the unorganised sector a frightening 77 per cent. i.e.840 millions of Indians live on a 
pathetic Rs. 20/-per day. This shows the depth and pervasiveness of poverty in 
India. Now, two per cent of world's richest own mor e than 50 per cent of global 
household wealth. 
When it comes to India, as per a report, there is a  perceptible increase in inter-
personal wealth inequality in India between 1991 and 2006. While the top 10 per cent 
of the population increased its share of total national wealth to 55 per cent, the share of 
the bottom 10 per cent fell, during the same period , to 0.21 per cent. The contrast 
between concentration of wealth at the very top and the prevalence of mass poverty, 
with the most appalling conditions of life at the b ottom, is shocking. It is morally 
indefensible and unacceptable. We have to deal with  the social and economic 
inequalities. So, I request the Government of India  to do this by reversing the rapid 
onslaught of "Second Partition" between the privileged classes and hundreds of millions 
of toiling masses of our country. Thank you. 
Demand for waiving off Service Tax on Computer Education  
SHRI SHANTARAM LAXMAN NAIK (Goa): Sir, seventy per cent of the 
graduates in India have a Degree either in Science or Arts or Commerce and a large 
number of them are seeking white-collar jobs. They are frustrated as they do not get 
necessary response to their applications for jobs f rom private and public sectors 
due to their deficiency in specialised technical education. 
One of the fast-growing sectors in today's society is information technology sector. 
Institutes have come up in the country, which train  students in various methods and 
procedures of computer applications. A student can pursue his career as system 
administrator, network engineer, solution provider, etc., through these institutes and 
can get direct job placements in the open market. 
We also find that the students are taking computer studies as one of the subjects 
in the vocational stream at the Higher Secondary School level and at the degree level. 
However, they acquire a limited knowledge at these levels. 
Students, after finishing 10th or 12th standard, ca n pursue computer education 
directly in computer educational institutes, and th ey can get direct job placements 
thereby avoiding the unnecessary 3 years degree cou rse as well as monetary 
liabilities. 
Fees charged by these institutes are reasonable but due to the service tax of 12.36 
per cent to be paid to the Central Government, the fees get inflated and it becomes a 
burden to those seeking knowledge in computer appli cations for obtaining 
employment. 

Special [21 NOV. 2007] Mentions    151 
The Central Government should, therefore, waive off the service tax in respect of 
computer institutes, which are operating in the country, as as a measure of eradicating 
unemployment. Thank you. 
Introduction of passenger trains on Bangalore-Hassan-Mangalore                            
Broad-gauge Railway Line 
SHRI JANARDHANA POOJARY (Karnataka): Sir, it is my pleasure to raise a 
Special Mention regarding introduction of passenger  trains on Bangalore-Hassan-
Mangalore broad-gauge railway line. 
This is in connection with the Announcement made by the hon. Minister of State for 
Railways, Shri R. Velu, that passenger train services on the Bangalore-Hassan-Mangalore 
broad-gauge railway line would commence in the month of November, 2007. Recently, 
the General Manager, South Western Railway, announced that the railway line was 
complete with due clearance from the Commissioner of Railway Safety, after addressing 
certain concerns expressed by the Railway Board authorities. Yet, there is no sign of 
passenger train services on the section. It is reported that plying of passenger trains on the 
Bangalore-Hassan-Mangalore section is delayed merely because the Railway Board has 
so far not given its green signal for the same. It may be mentioned that good-trains are 
plying on the Bangalore-Hassan-Mangalore broad-gauge railway line for the last few 
months. 
The people of Karnataka have been waiting for years for completion of the gauguage 
convernsion of the Bangalore-Hassan-Mangalore secti on and operationalisation of 
passenger trains thereon. When commissioned, it would boost the economic development 
of the region. 
The inordinate delay in operationising passenger tr ain services on this line has 
already spurred violent agitations on a number of times earlier. Any further delay is bound to 
be chaotic, since the railway line is ready for commissioning. I, therefore, urge upon the 
Central Government to immediately commission passenger train services on the Bangalore-
Hassan-Mangalore broad-gauge railway line. Thank you.

Need to take effective steps for Merger of Four                                                           
Public Sector Insurance Companies in National Interest 
SHRI. M.V. MYSURA REDDY (Andhra Pradesh): Mr. Deputy Chairman, Sir, the 
Government is aware that the four public sector general insurance companies such as the 
National Insurance Company Ltd., the New India Insurance Company Ltd., the Oriental 
Insurance Company Ltd. and the United India Insuran ce Company Ltd. have been 
rendering yeoman service to the people of the country by offering various policies for 
their benefits and also providing necessary funds for social development. During the 
year 1999, the Government amended the Insurance Act, 1938 allowing private insurance 
companies to operate its functions in different parts of the country including foreign 
insurance companies also. In the year 2002, the holding company of the four public 
sector general insurance companies, viz., the General Insurance Corporation of India was 
delinked and made a separate entity limiting its role to reinsurance business in the country. 
After the Insurance Act was amended, eight private companies entered into the filed of general 
insurance market. Competing with the private companies, the above four public sector 
general insurance companies have performed well. But the companies are doing similar 
services to the people. The service conditions are same in the four organisations. 
The UPA Government committed itself in the National Common Minimum Programme 
that the Central Government would strengthen the public sector insurance. But it is a matter of 
grave concern that the Government has done nothing towards fulfilling its commitment. The 
merger of

public sector and it will help the Government to in vest more in social sector due to 
increased mobilization of people's savings and prov iding employment to the 
unemployed youths.

the four public sector general insurance companies in the national interest. Thank 
you.
